That table is the unit's own list of what it moves and decides which vehicles this trainer offers. Dimensions are converted from the millimetres it states to centimetres; a figure it gives as "—" or "d/ý", and a weight it gives as a range, stay unavailable rather than being filled in from elsewhere. Securing hardware is only ever the handbook's (Order 145/175-ö, Annex 14, Tables 11 and 13), carried across for the vehicles it actually names.

vehicles.class: Main battle tank (esasy söweş tanky) — T-72 "Ural", the service name of Object 172M; the handbook covers it as Object 172
vehicles.notes: THE HANDBOOK DOES COVER THIS VEHICLE, under its factory designation. Annex 14's Table 13 lists 'Object 172' inside the grouped entry veh-obj-family-137 (Objects 137, 155, 166, 172, 608 and the engineer vehicles beside them) and assigns that whole group iron spur type Ş-137. Object 172M is the T-72, so its securing method is not a choice: para. 31 mandates the iron spur, and the spur type comes from the handbook by name. That identification is the one thing here that is NOT from the handbook — the extract never writes the name 'T-72' — and it is why this record exists separately instead of the family entry being renamed, which the project's own rule forbids. The dimensions are the manufacturer's published specification for the baseline T-72: hull 6.86 m (9.53 m over the gun trained forward), 3.59 m wide, 2.19 m to the turret roof, 41.0 t, 0.47 m ground clearance, 580 mm track shoes, 4.27 m of track bearing on the ground. Those last two give a nominal ground pressure of 0.83 kg/cm2 against para. 51's 0.8 — the published figure agrees. At 41.0 t it sits inside Table 8's 25.1-42 t bracket, so KGUUB-2G would cover it, but the named spur assignment governs. Dimensions, width, height and weight are from the vehicle transport-characteristics table. Any further figure on this record — ground clearance, track width, track contact length, axle count — is not in that table and was carried from the earlier catalogue entry for this same vehicle, where it came from the manufacturer specification or the design mockup. It is not handbook data. Length, width, height and weight are from the vehicle transport-characteristics table, whose weight column does not say whether the figure is a combat, kerb or transport weight, so it is recorded with its basis unstated. Any further figure on this record — ground clearance, track width, track contact length, axle count — is not in that table and was carried from the earlier catalogue entry for this same vehicle, where it came from the manufacturer specification or the design mockup. It is not handbook data.

vehicles.class: Main battle tank (esasy söweş tanky) — T-90S, the export variant of the T-90; built under licence in India as the "Bhishma". Not a handbook entry
vehicles.notes: NOT A HANDBOOK VEHICLE. The handbook's Annex 14 catalogue stops at the Soviet-era types and never names a T-90 of any variant, so no securing method is assigned to this machine by name and none may be inferred from the tables that are. The figures here are the manufacturer's published specification for the T-90S export tank: hull 6.86 m (9.53 m overall with the gun trained forward), 3.78 m over the side skirts, 3.37 m over the tracks, 2.23 m to the turret roof, 46.5 t combat weight, 0.49 m ground clearance, 580 mm track shoes, and 4.27 m of track bearing on the ground (recorded as both the road-wheel base and, separately, as trackContactLengthCm, which is what the para. 51 ground-pressure limit is computed on: 46.5 t over 2 x 58 cm x 427 cm = 0.94 kg/cm2, against that paragraph's 0.8 kg/cm2 — the published nominal figure of 0.938 kg/cm2 agrees). The securing hardware listed is the handbook's own general provision for a tracked vehicle on an open wagon (wood stop blocks and wire lashings, para. 32), not a per-vehicle assignment. At 46.5 t the vehicle is above Table 8's 42 t KGUUB coverage, so approved method 1 does not apply to it, and above the 15 t special case for side-ramp loading in para. 51. Dimensions, width, height and weight are from the vehicle transport-characteristics table. Any further figure on this record — ground clearance, track width, track contact length, axle count — is not in that table and was carried from the earlier catalogue entry for this same vehicle, where it came from the manufacturer specification or the design mockup. It is not handbook data. Length, width, height and weight are from the vehicle transport-characteristics table, whose weight column does not say whether the figure is a combat, kerb or transport weight, so it is recorded with its basis unstated. Any further figure on this record — ground clearance, track width, track contact length, axle count — is not in that table and was carried from the earlier catalogue entry for this same vehicle, where it came from the manufacturer specification or the design mockup.
